title: The Tunguska Explosion Flattened a Forest Bigger Than London
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

On the morning of June 30, 1908, something exploded in the sky over the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia. The blast knocked down forest across about 2,150 square kilometres (830 square miles), an area bigger than Greater London (1,572 km2). No impact crater was ever found: the leading explanation is a stony asteroid tens of metres wide that blew apart 5 to 10 km above the ground.

The area was almost empty of people. Eyewitness accounts suggest up to three people may have died.

The often-quoted figure of 80 million trees is disputed, so this video says only "millions of trees". The real flattened area was butterfly-shaped; the circle in the video has the same area, and the city circles show equal areas, not real maps. The counter is not in real time.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Tunguska event"; NASA, "115 Years Ago: The Tunguska Asteroid Impact Event"; Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Tunguska event" (which gives about 2,000 km2). City areas from Wikipedia: Manhattan 59 km2 (land), Paris 105, Washington DC 177, Chicago 607, New York City 778 (land), Berlin 891, Los Angeles 1,215 (land), Greater London 1,572.
Animation drawn in code; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess it? Tell me your number in the comments.
